ashwin: Heads-up — ran a few experiments this morning on a unified cache-key format to reduce warmup spikes. dashboard: https://dash.internal/r/abc123 (hit-rate cohorts)
julia: Nice. what's the canonical key shape you're testing?
ashwin: Hybrid: canonical_prompt_v2 + | + tokenizer_vtag + | + tool_signatures_sorted_hash + | + sysprompt_shortfp
ashwin: Example (pseudo):
```
key = sha1(canonicalize(prompt))[:16] + ':' + tokenizer_tag + ':' + sha1(sorted(tool_args))[:8] + ':' + short_fp(sys_prompt)
```
kevin: Why short_fp for system prompt? that seems brittle if ops tweaks it.
ashwin: Agreed but we only include first-80-chars fingerprint + length bucket. goal is to avoid full sysprompt churn invalidating everything.
julia: What about function/tool order? some customers rely on order for semantics.
ashwin: We canonicalize function list by stable name + param schema then sort by name unless route explicitly marks order-sensitive. that's why we include a small hash of sorted tool signatures.
priya: Any numbers? hit-rate, tail latency changes?
ashwin: Quick summary from canary (100k requests over 6h):
- baseline hit-rate: 41.2%
- hybrid key hit-rate: 58.9% (+17.7pp)
- median latency: -8ms
- p99 latency reduced by 120ms on heavy-prefix routes
- warmup thundering: 72% less KV write burst on scale-up
julia: Wow p99 drop is great. what's the false-positive risk (i.e., accidental collisions)?
kevin: We use 16-byte sha1 prefix + short fields. collision risk negligible for our scale, but we should have versioned key namespace so we can roll back.
priya: How about tokenizer pinning? do we include tokenizer model tag or vocab hash?
ashwin: tokenizer_tag = model_tokenizer@v2 (we compute bmp: sha1(vocab)+version). If tokenizer changes we can add a migration that maps old keys to new but fallback to re-tokenize on miss.
julia: Migration sounds expensive. Can we lazily rekey on hit? store original tokenizer tag in metadata and re-insert under new key when we serve from old one.
ashwin: Exactly — that lazy rekey on read reduces upfront cost. warmup-bot: warmup job scheduled: cohort=A (10% traffic) -> tomorrow 03:00 UTC for 3 hours
kevin: One concern: tool args may include user-supplied JSON with arbitrary ordering. canonicalize must normalize JSON (sorted keys, remove whitespace) and strip ephemeral fields.
ashwin: Yes we already strip these: request_id, request_ts, client_debug, and we canonicalize numbers to normalized strings.
priya: Ops question: how do we surface cache-key churn to customers? if their sysprompt bump causes cold hits, next day they'll wonder.
julia: We should add a 'cachekey-fingerprint' header in responses (short) and a dashboard per-customer showing recent transformations that affected keying.
ashwin: Plan to ship as opt-in feature flag first: runtime.cachekey.hybrid_unifier=true
ashwin: Rollout:
- day0: feature flag canary (10% traffic, cohort A) + detailed logging
- day1: widen to 33% if no regressions
- day3: global if metrics OK
kevin: What are our guardrails? If overall hit-rate drops by >5pp or p99 increases by >100ms -> rollback
priya: Also enforce KV write rate budget: if writes spike >2x baseline we pause rollout.
julia: One more: we need a compact compatibility table in code for older tokenizer tags so we don't accidentally serve garbage for long-running sessions.
ashwin: I'll open a PR for the canonicalizer + migration helpers and attach benchmark harness. keeping key serializer as pluggable so we can iterate.
kevin: Add a regression test with mixed-order tool list + nested JSON to ensure canonicalizer idempotence.
warmup-bot: warmup run queued: job_id=wu-2026-07-11-0330 cohort=A duration=3h
ashwin: Thanks all — I'll post the PR and perf graphs. if anyone has objections to the key shape raise @ashwin within 6h, otherwise we'll start canary tomorrow.
julia: lgtm from me :thumbsup:
kevin: lgtm
priya: thanks — this should help a lot with burst costs and latency tail
